s1_terminal: Earth is healthy. Why choose to leave?
Asteria is a beginning. What could you build there?
What do you want? What do you need? Choose one object from Earth.
s1_boarding: One looks back. One steps forward. One hides their nerves.
Cross the threshold together. What did the audience see before anyone spoke?
s1_launch: The restraints lock. Take one last breath of Earth.
Ignition. Vibration. Pressure. Earth falls beneath you.
The cities are still lit. Everything familiar grows smaller.
Engine cutoff. A pen lifts. Not everyone laughs.
s1_habitation: Meet Juno, Chief Rhee and Dr Okafor.
Which place will matter to your department? Why?
What would make this ship feel like your home?
What does your Earth object hold that the ship cannot replace?
s1_observation: The glass darkens. The stars brighten. Watch in silence.
Bent light. Less than a second. Then it is gone.
Write three lines: a visible action, dialogue and a silent reaction.
s1_route: Keep your Earth object. Keep the question open.
s2_recreation: Bad food. Missing equipment. An argument over a booking.
What does each character want? Show what they do to get it.
s2_malfunction: A maintenance unit welds a perfectly functional door shut.
That unit is either malfunctioning or developing artistic opinions. Both are unacceptable.
s2_encounter: Protect the ship and its people. Choose a safe way to stop the repairs.
A drone welds the door. Show preparation, action and reaction.
Another drone dismantles life support. Change your tactic.
PLEASE DO NOT INTERFERE WITH YOUR PREVIOUS REPAIR.
Shutdown, retreat or containment. The record survives.
s2_record: Rhee opens the service history. His expression changes.
Machines lie less often than people. That does not mean they never lie.
Write 6–8 lines: event, choice and consequence. Begin with a gesture.
s2_restricted: All access attempts are logged and reviewed.
Has your trust changed? Keep the maintenance record.
s3_observation: Investigate together. Report a FACT, an INFERENCE and a QUESTION.
A fact shows evidence. An inference explains it. A question stays open.
s3_evidence: 37 days or 102 days. The route has not changed.
K-17 mass and lensing readings do not fit normal physics.
The clocks work correctly. They no longer agree.
Cells and biological clocks drift differently from ship time.
s3_council: State one FACT. Keep theories separate.
What do we know? What do we think? What should we observe next?
If the instrument is wrong, tell me how. If physics is wrong, I need a longer lunch.
Your cells do not know they are supposed to agree with the ship clock.
s3_iris: Estimated time to Asteria: thirty-seven days.
Navigation says one hundred and two.
Correct according to what frame of reference?
s3_lensing: K-17 catches the observation window. Watch the starlight.
The same almost-human geometry. This time, more people see it.
What did you see? Which part is still an inference?
s3_craft: Replay the exchange. Change pace, pause, pitch, volume or emphasis.
Write what you KNOW, what you THINK and one QUESTION.
s3_packet: A packet arrives through deep-space communications.

dialogue_captions.Because humanity should never have only: Earth is healthy. We choose to build a second civilization on Asteria-4.
dialogue_captions.We will disagree. When we do, speak plai: Speak plainly. Listen closely. Make your reasons clear.
dialogue_captions.Then give your character something to do: Show your nerves through an action: a tightened strap or a folded note.
dialogue_captions.Who crosses first? Who hangs back? Who n: You can disagree and still cross the same line.
Asteria-4. A deliberate second civilization. Earth remains habitable.
Flight. Science. Engineering. Colony. Each depends on the others.
dialogue_captions.Keep the observation separate from the e: Tell us what you measured. Then explain what you think it means.
